note: One measured success and the four ways this route can answer with no profile on it. Each is a different fact and none of them is the others: a username nobody holds is the origin saying so, a payload whose container moved is the shape changing under a K1 client, a 200 that is not JSON is this route no longer answering in JSON, and 401 is the origin's own refusal. The one that matters most is the login page: it says 'Log in' in plain words at HTTP 200, and reading that as a refusal is the false negative the LinkedIn measurement overturned. Only a status line may make this route auth_required.

cases.evidence: measured: 200, 455 KB in 2.9 s, carrying username, biography, followers, post count and 12 recent posts each with shortcode, taken_at_timestamp, like count and comment count

the one empty this route can honestly answer with: the container is there and holds a null where a profile would be, which is the origin stating that nobody holds the name. Typing it as drift would send an operator hunting a payload change every time a handle was misspelled
spec Risks, structured-data drift: a K1 payload the vendor may reshape without notice. A profile that is somewhere else is not a profile that is not there

a 200 carrying words that look like a wall. What is true of it is that this route answered in something other than JSON; what is not true is that a credential was withheld, and only the origin's status line may say that
the sharpest form of the rule, and the same bytes as the row above: at 200 the body decides nothing and at 401 the status line decides everything
